answer: To resist Sybil attacks, networks deploy game-theoretic multi-agent auditing using topological cut verifications. Agents route trust flows across graphs, tagging fraudulent nodes like an identifiable pigment. Auditing coalitions verify cuts separating isolated clusters; if collusion occurs, stake slashing burns security deposits. Across sparse connectivity, forging cuts scales attacker cost at a superlinear rate, whether nodes dock at a digital wharf or freeze out sybils across an uncooperative data tundra.
